div.head: ECf 32 B 12
div.ab: Debet etiam in Londoniis, que caput regni est et legum et semper curia domini regis, singulis septimanis die Lune husting sedere et teneri.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 657 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 B …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann marks “caput” with a dagger for his marginal reference to Hn 87, 5.

note.seg: Hn gab Wessex diesen Ehrenrang, den auch andere Londoner damals sich vindiciren: o. S. 587q und vgl. Will. f. Steph.: Londonia regni Anglorum sedes. Die Sätze 12 f. citirt Londons Liber albus in Monum. Gildh. ed. Riley I 497 f.

Hn gave Wessex this rank of honour, which other Londoners too claimed for themselves at the time: above, p. 587, note q, and cf. Will. f. Steph.: Londonia regni Anglorum sedes. London’s Liber albus quotes sentences 12 f., in Monum. Gildh., ed. Riley I 497 f.

div.ab: Also in London, which is the head of the kingdom and of the laws, and always the court of the lord king, the husting must sit and be held every week on Monday.
